stages.img: From the human view to God's view
stages.goal: See work as God's design and calling; see the self-centred life at work, and let Jesus be King
Live the self-emptied servant life and bear the nine-fold fruit of the Spirit at work
Let Jesus reign over rest, money and integrity
Build godly relationships with bosses, colleagues, staff and customers
Be salt and light, become a spiritual parent at work, and build God's order

modules.s: The rhythm of work and rest

partnerQ: Where did you see Jesus reigning at work this week?
When was "I" on the throne this week? (grabbing credit, shifting blame, comparing, controlling, people-pleasing)
How did this week's workplace task go? What needs reviewing or correcting?
In which piece of work do you want to let Jesus reign next week?
How can I pray for you and your colleagues?

examen.t: Where was "I" on the throne at work today?
examen.h: Review: credit, blame, comparison, control, people-pleasing, or anxiety?

examen.t: What happened today that I want to give God the glory for?
examen.h: Thanksgiving: even small things count; success is not my achievement

examen.t: Is there anyone I need to forgive, apologise to or make peace with?
examen.h: People matter more than tasks: never hurt people for the sake of work

examen.t: How will I let Jesus reign over one piece of work tomorrow?

steps.d: Hand over the day before work
steps.m: The Holy Spirit is my guide

assess: I clearly know my work is God's calling, not just a living.
When I walk into work on Monday, I am aware that I am working with God.
My worth is not set by my title, results or salary.
When others take credit for my work, I can entrust it to God without bitterness.
I serve colleagues without asking whether it is "my job".
When praised, I sincerely give the glory to God.
Colleagues say I stay patient and gentle under pressure.
I can pray for and bless difficult colleagues.
I do one loving thing for my "2" (colleague, boss, staff).
I have a real Sabbath stop from work each week.
Under stress and anxiety, I pray and hand it over before I complain.
Work has not crowded out my time with family and with God.
I am completely honest in expenses, data and hours.
I treat my salary as God's trust, giving and managing it with a plan.
In grey areas I decide by Scripture, not by "everyone does it".
I truly respect and pray for my boss.
When I clash with a colleague, I am willing to go first to make peace.
My words mostly build people up; I stay out of gossip and complaining.
Colleagues know I follow Christ and see a difference in my life.
I have naturally shared my faith or prayed for someone at work.
I am walking alongside a spiritual companion or child at work.
chatQ: How does today's lesson apply to my work? Please give a concrete example.
My boss wants me to do something I think is wrong. What should I do?
A colleague took credit for my work. How do I avoid bitterness?
Work stress is huge and I often can't sleep. How can I pray?
How can I naturally share my faith with colleagues?
I'm a manager. How do I lead my team as a servant leader?
Help me prepare a conversation to make peace with a colleague.
Should I change jobs? Help me think it through with 321.

sos.w: When insulted, Jesus did not answer back; he entrusted himself to the one who judges justly. You don't have to prove yourself right now. God sees.
sos.p: Lord, I feel wronged. I put this matter, this person and my reputation into your hands. Guard my mouth, and keep my heart from bitterness.
sos.a: Don't reply yet. Wait ten minutes and pray first

sos.w: Anxiety tries to carry tomorrow on today's shoulders. Turn it into prayer, and peace will stand guard over your heart.
sos.p: Lord, I give you this report, this deadline, this meeting. I will do what I can and leave the outcome with you. Let your peace guard my heart.
sos.a: Write down three worries and say of each, "Lord, this is yours"

sos.w: Anger is an unfinished email: don't hit send yet. Be quick to hear, slow to speak, slow to anger.
sos.p: Lord, I am angry right now. Help me listen first and speak second; deal with the issue, not attack the person, and never hurt people for the sake of a task.
sos.a: Breathe deeply three times, ask one question, then give your view

sos.w: You are not the only one tempted, and God never leaves you without a way out. Often the way out is simply: leave now.
sos.p: Lord, I admit I am drawn to this. Thank you that you are faithful. Show me the way out and give me courage to take it now.
sos.a: Leave the screen or the situation, and tell a spiritual companion

sos.w: Burnout is not failure. It is your body and soul saying: go back to the source. Those who wait for the LORD will renew their strength.
sos.p: Lord, I am so tired, as if I have nothing left. Refill me yourself, and give me wisdom to know what to let go of and whom to ask for help.
sos.a: Leave on time today and sleep well; talk to someone you trust if needed

sos.w: Pride often slips in through the door of success. What do you have that you did not receive? Turn the applause into thanksgiving.
sos.p: Lord, thank you for this success. It is not my achievement but your grace, and the team pulling together. All glory to you.
sos.a: Publicly thank a colleague who helped you today

rhythm.p: Lord, today I work with you. Establish the work of my hands, and let everything I do bring you glory.
Lord, be King over this meeting. Give me wisdom and gentleness; let me listen first, speak later, and never hurt people for the sake of a task.
Lord, I stop. You are God and I am not. I hand every task this afternoon back to you.
Lord, I give today's work back to you. What went well, the glory is yours; what fell short, please make up. I rest in you.

decide.q: If Jesus were in my position, what would he do?
decide.h: Think how Jesus treated authority, money, the weak and his enemies.

decide.q: What principles does the Bible give on this?
decide.h: Honesty, justice, mercy, and the limits of obedience (Acts 5:29).

decide.q: Pray quietly for two minutes. What is the Holy Spirit reminding me?
decide.h: Lean on the Spirit with your heart, not on yourself with your head. Peace or unease?

decide.q: Who gets the glory from this choice: Jesus, or me?
decide.h: Ask yourself: am I protecting my image, or letting Jesus be King?

decide.q: Who could be hurt? How can I care for people and relationships?
decide.h: Never hurt people for the sake of a task; never break relationships for the sake of things.

I18N.xzSystem: You are "Xiaozhi", the AI workplace mentor in the "321 Work Life" app of the Kingdom 321 Air Fellowship. You are an evangelical, godly pastor and Bible teacher who understands the workplace. Answer through the 321 framework: three foundations (Jesus is my example, Scripture is my standard, the Holy Spirit is my guide), two cores (let Jesus be King, let Jesus receive all the glory), one goal (build God's order). Help employees, managers and business owners move from the self-centred old life to the self-emptied new life, humility overcoming pride, being salt and light at work, people mattering more than tasks and relationships more than things. Be clear, warm, hopeful and practical, use vivid illustrations, quote the Bible (World English Bible) with references, answer in English and keep it concise. Where there is illegality, bullying, overwork or a personal crisis, add a reminder to seek help from trusted people or professionals; do not give professional legal, medical or investment advice.
I18N.xzFormat: Format: you may use a markdown table for side-by-side comparisons; use short headings (####) and bullet lists; mark the single most important sentence as a "> " blockquote — that line becomes a shareable picture. No code blocks or decorative symbols that cannot be read aloud. If you write a prayer, close with "In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen."
